planting.note: Grafted or rooted-cutting starts establish fastest once nights stay reliably above 60°F.

directions: Root softwood cuttings or graft onto vigorous obesum rootstock, then keep the compact caudex-forming plant in fast-draining mineral mix. Withhold water in cool months to force dormancy and trigger heavier bloom flushes. Feed lightly with a low-nitrogen, high-phosphorus fertilizer through the warm growing season. Expect double flowers with red-purple petals surrounding a white throat blotch.
sources: USPTO Plant Patent USPP24852P3, 'Adenium plant named LEELADE202'

planting.note: Best propagated from grafted scion wood in late spring once greenhouse or outdoor temperatures hold warm overnight.

directions: Grow in a gritty, fast-draining substrate and graft or root cuttings from healthy stock to preserve the doubled deep-red flower form. Reduce irrigation sharply in cooler months so the plant can enter a natural rest period. Provide maximum direct sun and warmth to encourage the large, layered blooms typical of this selection. Repot every one to two years as the caudex thickens.
sources: USPTO Plant Patent USPP24883P3, 'Adenium plant named LEELADE204'

planting.note: A compact grower, so it suits container culture even where garden space is limited.

directions: Propagate by stem cuttings or grafting to keep the deep-red, greyed-purple-margined double flowers true to type. Use a mineral-heavy potting mix and let the soil dry fully between waterings to prevent stem rot. Keep the thickened caudex partly exposed above the soil line for display and easier moisture monitoring. Cut back on fertilizer and water once temperatures drop to allow winter dormancy.
sources: USPTO Plant Patent USPP24851P3, 'Adenium plant named LEELADE205'

planting.note: White-and-purple bicolor blooms show best contrast when the plant gets strong, unfiltered sun.

directions: Start new plants from cuttings or grafts taken from disease-free stock to retain the white, red-purple-margined double flower pattern. Plant in a coarse, well-aerated succulent mix and water only after the root zone dries completely. Provide bright, direct light for most of the day to maximize flowering and compact growth. Reduce watering substantially during cooler, low-light months.
sources: USPTO Plant Patent USPP24882P3, 'Adenium plant named LEELADE206'

planting.note: Vigorous, thick-stemmed selection that fills a 6-inch or larger container within its first growing season.

directions: Propagate from apical stem cuttings to preserve the vigorous upright habit and triple-petaled, dark-red-edged flowers with a bright yellow floral tube. Grow in a fast-draining container mix and let it dry out between waterings, especially through cooler months. Give it full sun and warm temperatures to support the thick main stem and large glossy leaves. Feed sparingly during active growth and stop fertilizing when the plant slows down in winter.
sources: USPTO Plant Patent USPP28731P2, 'Adenium plant named GEM-113-1', assigned to Florida Foundation Seed Producers, Inc.
